$comment: Canonical benchmark solver index. Maps the algorithm doc id (the join key used by teeline-web's `docs` collection and nav-data.ts) to the solver's canonical CLI name (`teeline solvers` NAME column / `Solvers::variants()`). Consumers: scripts/bench-matrix.sh (CLI invocation), scripts/publish-benchmarks.sh (criteriondb `solver` field + R2 shard filename), teeline-web/src/lib/solver-index.ts (per-algorithm page lookup). `deterministic` MUST come from measurement, not from reading the source, and each claim carries `determinism_evidence` so it can be re-derived. An unmeasured solver MUST be left deterministic:false — the UI then shows a median/spread instead of one authoritative number, which is the safe default. NOTE: solvers that auto-seed from `nn` inherit nn's variance.

solvers.name: Bellman–Held–Karp
solvers.notes: Exponential; only viable on very small instances (<= ~20 cities). Measured stable over 5-6 runs on a280 (n=280). Measured identical over 3 runs on burma14. Measured optimal on burma14/gr17/ulysses16. Measured identical across 3 process invocations on burma14/gr17/ulysses16.

solvers.name: Branch and Bound
solvers.notes: Default `n_nearest=3` restricts branching to the 3 nearest cities, which makes it a BEAM SEARCH, not an exact solver: measured burma14 3651 / gr17 2187 / ulysses16 6909 against known optima 3323 / 2085 / 6859. With `--n_nearest 100` it returns all three optima. Output is reproducible across runs (identical over 3 invocations of each instance). Benchmark both configs: `default` (n_nearest=3) and `exact` (--n_nearest 100).

solvers.name: Nearest Neighbour
solvers.notes: Non-deterministic today: `n_nearest` defaults to 3 and the frontier query is visited-blind, so the HashSet-iteration fallback in nearest_neighbor.rs picks a different city per process. Phase 1 of the plan fixes this.

solvers.name: Christofides
solvers.notes: <= 1.5x approximation guarantee. Measured stable over 5-6 runs on a280 (n=280). Measured identical over 5 runs on a280.

solvers.name: Greedy Edge
solvers.notes: Kruskal-style edge insertion with degree and sub-tour guards. Measured stable over 5-6 runs on a280 (n=280). Measured identical over 5 runs on a280.

solvers.name: Savings
solvers.notes: Clarke-Wright style savings construction. Measured stable over 5-6 runs on a280 (n=280). Measured identical over 5 runs on a280.

solvers.name: Fourier
solvers.notes: Measured: 2 runs on berlin52 agreed (8549.14), so treated as low-variance but not proven deterministic — repeat measurement required.

solvers.name: Kohonen SOM
solvers.notes: Self-organising map; CLI name is `kohonen_som`, doc id `som`.

solvers.name: 2-opt
solvers.notes: NON-DETERMINISTIC (measured). Auto-seeds from nn, so it inherits nn's variance: 6 runs on a280 gave 2814.92 / 3125.49 / 2797.03. Stable on berlin52 only by luck of that instance.

solvers.name: 3-opt
solvers.notes: NON-DETERMINISTIC (measured). Auto-seeds from nn: 2 runs on a280 gave 2690.56 / 2706.56.

solvers.name: Or-opt
solvers.notes: NON-DETERMINISTIC (measured). Auto-seeds from nn: 6 runs on a280 gave 2815.80 / 2886.48 / 2813.79 / 2884.47.

solvers.name: Lin-Kernighan
solvers.notes: Iterated local search with double-bridge kicks; reaches berlin52 optimum but varies run to run.

solvers.name: Stochastic Hill Climbing
solvers.notes: No CLI alias (`stochastic_hill` is the only spelling).

solvers.name: Simulated Annealing
solvers.notes: `--no-seed` switches from random shuffle to the input tour order.

solvers.name: Tabu Search
solvers.notes: Measured: 2 runs on berlin52 agreed (8980.92); treat as low-variance, re-measure.

solvers.name: Gravitational Search
solvers.notes: Education-oriented implementation; known to produce very large gaps.

solvers.name: Ant Colony
solvers.notes: Measured: 2 runs on berlin52 gave 7857.55 and 7549.29 — high variance.

solvers.name: Random Shuffle
solvers.notes: Baseline random tour; no algorithm doc page. Benchmarked as a reference floor, never rendered on an algorithm page.
